finding: Validator timing on the same host, the same bit-identical binary, pinned to CPU 2, with the producer's per-configuration keys (selected on the producer's medians, scored on new timings). Round 1 (3 repeats, part A all 36 configurations + part B one nonce-drawn configuration per cell x 17 keys): 6 of 9 decisions reproduced; 2^24 T = 16384 (0.911 [0.811, 1.009]), 2^28 T = 1024 (0.991 [0.970, 1.043]) and 2^32 T = 1024 (1.072 [0.954, 1.109]) unranked: the three cells where the producer's fixed-key control is also unranked. Round 2 (5 repeats, added after round 1 and reported separately): 8 of 9 (2^28 T = 1024 unranked, 0.943 [0.924, 1.140]). Pooled (8 repeats per key): 9 of 9 decisions reproduced; 2^24 0.768-0.845 (12 of 12 configurations below 1), 2^28 0.976-1.016 (T = 1024 0.980 [0.959, 0.999], faster by a hair), 2^32 1.107-1.216 (12 of 12 above 1). Every producer cell interval overlaps the pooled validator interval. Per-configuration ratios differ between sessions by a median of 5.1% (p90 14%, max 22%), more than the within-session A/A median single-repeat deviation (2.8%) and within the per-cell A/A rep0/rep1 intervals. The 2^24 'faster' and 2^32 'slower' directions reproduce; the 28 b T = 1024 magnitude does not (0.93 vs 0.98) and its decision is fragile.

With n = 4 configurations per cell, the protocol's bootstrap 95% interval of the median equals [min, max] of the 4 configuration ratios in all 9 cells (a resample has median equal to the maximum with probability 13/256 > 2.5%; the exact bootstrap over all 256 resamples gives the same bounds). A 'faster'/'slower' decision therefore means all 4 configurations on one side of 1 (two-sided sign-test p = 0.125 for one cell); the '95%' label is nominal. The size-level evidence is the strong part: 12 of 12 configurations below 1 at 2^24 and 12 of 12 above 1 at 2^32 in the producer's data (two-sided sign test p = 0.00049 each), 11 of 12 in validator round 1 and 12 of 12 in round 2 and pooled.

severity: pass, with method caveats to disclose
finding: No dead code: the mul, sqr, inv and padd loops are loop-carried dependency chains through black_box; the native and lookup loops accumulate into a value passed to black_box; at param 1.0 every loop runs 4x longer and the counters scale exactly (I 4,000,006, M 26,000,012, S 24,000,009 vs 1,000,006 / 6,500,012 / 6,000,009 at 0.25) while per-operation times stay nonzero and comparable. The padd chain is exactly one affine addition per step: the counters equal the expected I + 2M + S per step plus the two setup multiplications, so there was no doubling and no reset to G. Caveats: lookups are timed as independent probes (memory-level parallelism), not interleaved with dependent field arithmetic as in the harness; probes are 50% inserted keys and 50% uniform in [0, p), so at 24 bits with 2^22-2^24 inserted keys most 'misses' hit (2^24 random keys in [0, 2^24) are about 63% distinct) and the hit mix varies with size and curve; capacity is 2x the key count; single segments can be far off (validator run: one mul segment 28.8 ns against 7.3-7.8, giving I/M 6.0; producer 28 b 'after' padd 294 ns = 1.30x its I + 2M + S). The validator's 7 opcost runs reproduce the producer's ranges apart from that segment: GAE 209-267 ns, I/M 25-34, canonicalisation + hash 0.0055-0.0081 GAE, std lookup 0.047-0.144 (2^10-2^16) and 0.36-0.73 GAE (2^22-2^24).
